name: Grass Skirt
notes: Ivy wrapped around the waist for modesty.

name: Stone Tools
notes: Basic tools made using the process of knapping .

name: Rope
notes: The simplest form of rope using long twisted plant fibers.

name: Bow Drill
notes: Used for starting fires.

name: Fire
notes: A very important scientific tool.

name: Traps
notes: Used for snaring animals.

name: Pottery
notes: Used for storage.

name: Leather Hide
notes: Used for clothing. Made from deer skin.

name: Clothing
notes: Used for keeping warm.

name: Wicker Basket
notes: Used for storage.

name: Salt
notes: Used for flavoring and preserving food. Made by evaporating sea water.

name: Nitric Acid
notes: A highly corrosive mineral acid. [ 1 ] Found in the Cave of Miracles as a byproduct of bat guano. One of the main components used to make revival fluid.

name: Wine
notes: Wine made from crushing and fermenting red grapes for three weeks, stirring daily. Used as the alcohol source for making revival fluid after distillation.

name: Distillation Earthenware
notes: Used for purifying and concentrating alcohol.

name: Ethanol
notes: A simple alcohol that is flammable and can be used as a disinfectant. Distilled using the distillation earthenware to be used for making revival fluid.

name: Revival Fluid
notes: Also known as miracle fluid and the stone formula . Literally nital , an industrial-strength corrosive agent.

name: Fur Clothing
notes: Used for keeping slightly more warm.

name: Calcium Carbonate
notes: Made from crushed up seashells. Used in agriculture for getting rid of hydrogen ions in the soil, making it less acidic. [ 2 ] Used in making soap and mortar.

name: Mortar
notes: Used in construction as a predecessor to cement by heating it and mixing it with sand.

name: Soap
notes: Also known as dr. stone . Used for cleaning and getting rid of bacteria.

name: Sodium Carbonate
notes: Used in construction as a predecessor to cement by heating it and mixing it with sand.

name: Crossbow
notes: A ranged weapon similar to a bow that shoots arrows. Used ineffectively by Senku against Tsukasa, who caught the arrow in mid air.

name: Sextant
notes: A device used for determining global position based on the time.

name: Bronze
notes: Found in the Buddha of Kamakura. Used by Senku to improve his sextant's accuracy by making a mirror.

name: Raft
notes: A simple flotation device for traversing rivers.

name: Sulfur
notes: Chemical element with atomic number 16. Can be found naturally in hot springs and volcanic areas. Ingredient of black powder. It becomes strongly electrostatically charged when rubbed with leather, allowing it to be used in a sulfur ball electrostatic generator.

name: Potassium Nitrate
notes: Made using the nitric acid from the Cave of Miracles. Used in gunpowder.

name: Glucose
notes: A common sugar created by heating up alcohol, found in most plants. Used to enhance the gunpowder.

name: Gunpowder
notes: A chemical explosive. Used to deter Tsukasa, signal Kohaku, later to make the pulleys used to rescue Kohaku, and in a fake gun to scare Hyoga and his troops away.

name: Pulley
notes: A device used to lessen the effective weight of an object through rope tension. Used by Senku to lift a tree off of Kohaku, saving her.

name: Makeshift Chassis
notes: A motorless go-kart made by Senku out of the pulley parts.

name: Soap Bubbles
notes: Bubbles made by lathering soap and blowing through a closed hoop. Used to bewilder the village guards.

name: Electrostatic Generator
notes: A friction-based generator of static electricity using a sulfur sphere and rubbing. Rubbing with leather generates more electricity than with human skin.

name: Malachite (Cu2CO3(OH)2)&Chalcanthite
notes: Malachite is a green, copper carbonate hydroxide mineral that was used as a green pigment for much of history. Chalcanthite is a blue copper sulfate and can be used as a copper ore. Both are found near copper deposits.

name: Corundum
notes: A crystalline form of aluminum oxide, very hard (a 9.0 on the Mohs scale if pure). Tends to be used as an abrasive due to its hardness.

name: Galena
notes: The natural mineral form of lead(II) sulfide. An important source of silver ore. Much later used as semiconductor material in a crystal radio.

name: Cinnabar
notes: The natural mineral form of mercury(II) sulfide. The historic source of vermilion pigment, and a source of mercury. Due to the presence of mercury, cinnabar is toxic to humans.

name: Gold
notes: Chemical element with atomic number 79. Used in making Kinro's golden spear.

name: Golden Spear
notes: A really cool looking gold-tipped spear used to bribe Kinro.

name: Natural Magnet
notes: Also called a lodestone , a naturally magnetized piece of magnetite (Fe 3 O 4 ). Used to easily filter iron sand from the river. Used by Chrome as a primitive compass.

name: Iron Sand
notes: Iron mineral particles found in the river. Typically particles of magnetite.

name: Scale
notes: Used to weigh out ratios of carbon and iron sand to make metallic iron.

name: Blast Furnace (Level 1)
notes: A furnace for making iron. Air is pumped in via four bag bellows.

name: Bag Bellows
notes: Used for pumping air into the furnace.

name: Millet Flour
notes: Flour made from foxtail millet.

name: Sodium Hydroxide
notes: A highly caustic base and alkali that has several applications. Used in the ramen to add alkalinity and in the sulfa drug. Derived from wood ash, or alternatively from salt water electrolysis.

name: Potassium Carbonate
notes: Used in the ramen to add elasticity.

name: Millet Noodles
notes: Made from foxtail millet flour. Used in the ramen.

name: Ramen
notes: Made with various meats, wild bird egg, millet noodles and topped with spring onions.

name: Ramen Cart(ラーメン)
notes: A basic food cart for transporting and serving ramen from. Contains two stone furnaces for keeping the pots warms, a roof and a sign indicating the food type. Transported manually via two protruding handles and rolled on wheels (the repurposed pulleys made previously) like a traditional food cart .

name: Blast Furnace (Level 2)
notes: An improved furnace for making iron. Air is pumped in via four vertical shifting-type pumps.

name: Iron
notes: The most common element on Earth by mass. Used in countless Kingdom of Science creations.

name: Copper
notes: Used to make copper wire for the powerful magnet.

name: Copper Wire
notes: Made using molten copper, poured into a long groove in a plank stolen from the bridge into Ishigami Village. Used to make a magnet.

name: Lacquer
notes: An insulating coating made from the lacquer tree. Used on shields and on the magnet.

name: Lightning Rod
notes: Made from Kinro's golden spear, set atop Bald Mountain. Used to draw lightning to a specific spot to create the powerful magnet.

name: Strong Magnet
notes: A strong magnet, used in the generator.

name: Dual Hand-cranked Dynamo
notes: A man-powered electrical generator. Requires two people to turn the cranks in sync to generate power. Marks the beginning of electrical power use in the Kingdom of Science. Formally called Faraday's disk generator.

name: Bamboo Filament
notes: A baked piece of bamboo fiber used as a light bulb filament. Based off of Thomas Edison's bamboo filament lightbulbs. [ 3 ]

name: Candle
notes: A basic candle of liquid fat in a bowl with a simple wick.

name: Herbal Paste
notes: A paste of various medicinal plants, applied topically to Gen's injuries.

name: Teeth-Cleaning Twig
notes: A primitive toothbrush in the form of a twig that is chewed until one end is frayed and used to brush teeth. Some trees are better suited to clean and protect the teeth, due to the chemical composition of the plant parts. [ 4 ]

name: Quartz Sand
notes: Used to make glass.

name: Crystal Glass
notes: Glass made of powdered silica sand heated with burnt seaweed (20%) and calcium carbonate (10%), then some lead. Used in Suika's and Kinro's glasses.

name: Lens Polisher
notes: A man-powered whetstone bore for polishing and shaping the lenses for glasses.

name: Eye Chart
notes: A chart with simple shapes to test vision.

name: Melon Glasses
notes: Concave lens glasses using Suika's melon as frames.

name: Obsidian Foam Insulation
notes: A thermal insulator used to insulate the glassblowing furnace.

name: Leather Coveralls
notes: A thick leather garment made to protect the wearer from the heat of the furnace.

name: Glassblowing Tools
notes: A long iron straw for blowing into the glass to inflate it (formally called a blowpipe). Tongs for shaping bottlenecks. An annealing oven to slowly cool down finished pieces.

name: Glass Furnace
notes: A furnace for heating glass to working temperatures.

name: Laboratory Glassware
notes: A large selection of glass beakers and flasks for chemistry use in the lab, all made by Kaseki.

name: Native Silver
notes: Naturally occurring silver. Used in Ginro's silver spear to protect the group from sulfuric acid by reacting to the hydrogen sulfide.

name: Silver Spear
notes: A spear with a head coated in silver used for detecting hydrogen sulfide since it tarnishes black instantly (2Ag + H 2 S → Ag 2 S + H 2 ).

name: Activated Charcoal
notes: A form of carbon with an extremely high surface area due to a large amount of small, low-volume pores. Used in gas absorption for the gas masks.

name: Fire Lens
notes: A convex lens used to start fires by focusing sunlight into a point. Used by Chrome to start a fire in the grand bout. [ 5 ]

name: Gas Masks
notes: Masks used to defend against hydrogen sulfide by trapping and neutralizing it.

name: Sulfuric Acid
notes: A colourless acid used in many of Senku's inventions such as the sulfa drug and nitroglycerine.

name: Water Condenser
notes: A drip machine for capturing gases and condensing them into a liquid.

name: Hydrochloric Acid
notes: A colorless acid used in the sulfa drug.

name: Flowers of Sulfur
notes: A yellow sulfur powder produced by sublimation and deposition. Could also be geyserite as it is described as a white powder found near hot springs.

name: Condensing Column
notes: A cooled tube used for condensing gases into liquid.

name: Chlorosulfuric Acid
notes: A corrosive and harmful colorless liquid used in making the sulfa drug.

name: Ammonia
notes: A pungent colorless gas used in making the sulfa drug. Derived from urine.

name: Power-up Science Drink
notes: A concoction designed to enhance physical performance. Includes honey to increase blood sugar, camellia for caffeine and sweet flag to cool you down (possibly as a sedative).

name: Acetic Acid
notes: Also known as vinegar , derived from alcohol (ethanol) reacting with oxygen in the air. Turned into ketene in an iron pipe before becoming acetic anhydride. The glacial form (without water) was used in the sulfa drug

name: Water Carbonator
notes: A rotating drum with the excess carbon dioxide from fermentation being bubbled through. Probably based on the original design by Joseph Priestly. [ 6 ]

name: Tar(C + Other Hydrocarbons)
notes: A dark brown or black viscous liquid that can be made from coal, wood, petroleum, or peat.

name: Ethyl Acetate
notes: A colourless liquid with a slightly sweet smell.

name: Aniline
notes: A dangerous organic compound.

name: Carbonated Water
notes: Water with small amounts of carbon dioxide dissolved inside, creating carboxylic acid.

name: Acetic Anhydride
notes: The simplest isolable anhydride of a carboxylic acid, widely used as a reagent in organic synthesis.

name: Acetanilide
notes: A member of the class of acetamides.

name: Para-Acetamidobenzenesulfonic Acid(C8H9NO4S) & Para-Acetamidobenzenesulfonyl Chloride
notes: Part of the process of making the sulfa drug.

name: Sodium Bicarbonate
notes: Also known as baking soda , it is a white salt usually used in baking as a leavening agent.

name: Sulfanilamide
notes: The completed sulfa drug.

name: Cola
notes: A bottle of cola left by Senku for Gen as thanks.

name: Wire-Framed Glasses
notes: Pre-petrification style glasses with thin frames made for Kinro.

name: Katana
notes: Japanese-style swords made of sharpened steel with flexible spines. Made from iron that's been folded and forge welded into itself several times to draw out impurities. Pine ash gives off purple flames when temperature reaches 1200 degrees, making it a good temperature indicator. Painting the spine of the blade with dilute clay allows tempering of the cutting edge while keeping the spine soft, producing a blade that is flexible and durable while also being very sharp.

name: Small Knife
notes: A small, very sharp knife delivered to Gen, able to be easily palmed for sneaky cutting.

name: Crystalized Sugar
notes: Raw sugar crystals made by reducing yam liquor and mirin. Used in the cotton candy.

name: Wire Centrifuge
notes: A metal drum with small holes that spins, using the centrifugal force to push a molten substance inside through small holes, creating thin strands. Used to make cotton candy and gold wire.

name: Cotton Candy Machine
notes: Used to make cotton candy and gold wire.

name: Cotton Candy
notes: A sweet, fluffy treat.

name: Gear
notes: A gear made from Kohaku's shield to consistently spin things such as the record player and cotton candy machine. It allows to increase the speed of rotation.

name: Saw
notes: An improved version of the stone saws Kaseki was using, forged of iron.

name: Water Wheel
notes: A device for converting the energy of flowing or falling water into useful forms of power.

name: Hydroelectric Power Plant
notes: The water wheel coupled with the electric generator, allowing to charge batteries and power electrical loads without resorting to muscle power. Besides the generator, other machines such as bellows have been attached to the waterwheel for a power source.

name: Lead-acid Battery
notes: A lead-sulfuric acid battery, used for storing the power from the water wheel and act as a portable source of electricity, such as for mining lamps and vacuum tube filaments in wireless telephones. The oldest rechargeable battery, invented in 1859.

name: Reciprocating Rack and Pinion
notes: A type of gear mechanism that converts circular movement to back-and-forth movement.

name: Blast Furnace (Level 3)
notes: An even more improved furnace for making iron. Air is pumped in via a multiple cylinder horizontal reciprocating pump, powered by the water wheel.

name: Pickling
notes: A method of preserving food in an edible, antimicrobial liquid using airtight containers. The precursor to canning.

name: Vacuum Pump
notes: A device that uses mercury to remove the air from the inside of a light bulb. Historically known as a Sprengel pump.

name: Electric Light
notes: An incandescent light bulb that uses a carbonized bamboo or tungsten filament.

name: Light Switch
notes: A simple switch that connects or breaks an electrical circuit, allowing electrity to flow ("on" state) or not ("off" state).

name: Head Lamp
notes: A battery-powered light worn on the head to keep the hands free.

name: Copper Tube
notes: A tube that will expand inwards rather than outwards when heated, preventing the bulbs shattering.

name: Scheelite
notes: An ore of tungsten that glows blue under ultraviolet light.

name: Mica
notes: A group of minerals which can easily be split into extremely thin elastic plates.

name: Siphon
notes: A device which causes a liquid to flow upward, above the surface of a reservoir, with no pump, but powered by the fall of the liquid as it flows down the tube under the pull of gravity.

name: Pickaxe
notes: A metal tool used for prying, especially useful for mining.

name: Manganese Dioxide
notes: Used for making carbon-zinc batteries. Found in the skarn deposit.

name: Chalcopyrite (CuFeS2)&Sphalerite ((Zn,Fe)S)
notes: Chalcopyrite is the most important ore of copper, a good conductor. Sphalerite is the most important ore of zinc, useful in galvanization (preventing rust). Sphalerite's phosphorescence also makes it suitable for the screens in cathode ray tubes, producing a green glow.

name: Telescope
notes: An optical instrument that uses lenses to observe distant objects.

name: Tungsten Paste
notes: The uncooked version of the tungsten filament used in vacuum tubes and light bulbs.(WO 3 ). The process involves smashing the scheelite to dust, simmering in sodium hydroxide, adding seashells, hydrochloric acid and ammonia to make it crystalize then baking it and mixing it with honey.

name: All-in-one Heating Set
notes: A heating setup to bake the tungsten paste thus sintering it into a solid metal wire, using every bit of heat energy Chrome could possibly harness.

name: Electrolyzer
notes: A device used to pass electricity through water, extracting the hydrogen.

name: Tungsten Filament
notes: A filament with a very high melting point for use in vacuum tubes and long-lasting light bulbs. Because of the challenge of melting tungsten, the filament is instead made by microscopically welding powdered tungsten particles, a process known as sintering, and which requires a much lower temperature.

name: Methanol
notes: Also known as wood alcohol , can be made through the destructive distillation of wood. Used to make formalin.

name: Formalin
notes: Also known as aqueous formaldehyde , used to make bakelite plastic or to preserve bodies.

name: Gold Wire
notes: Conductive wire used for electronic devices.

name: Stove
notes: A device in which fuel is burned to heat either the space in which the stove is situated, or items placed on the heated stove or inside it in an oven.

name: Zinc-Manganese Battery
notes: Some of the batteries used to power the cell phone, specifically the anode supply for the vacuum tube. For their construction method, see Kung Dang Manganese .

name: Hickman Pump
notes: An upgraded vacuum pump used to achieve a very high vacuum required by vacuum tubes. A type of oil diffusion pump.

name: Phenolic Resin Plastic
notes: One of a variety of phenol formaldehyde resin plastics that are lightweight and can be moulded into shapes, besides being electrical insulators. The resin may be mixed with additives such as wood fibers to make the phenolic paper historically used as the substrate in circuit boards, or with wood flour to make Bakelite , used to make casings and other parts in electronics such as telephones and radios from the 1930's through the 1950's. It is the oldest fully synthetic plastic, and it's thermosetting, meaning once it hardens after being made, it cannot be remelted.

name: Vacuum Tube
notes: A device that controls electric current flow in a high vacuum between electrodes to which an electric potential difference has been applied. It can be used to amplify sound signals, as well as build oscillators to broadcast radio waves and many other uses. The early tubes made by the kingdom of science are called triodes, having three elements, a tungsten cathode that heats up with electricity and boils off electrons, a metal plate or anode placed nearby to catch those electrons, and a metal grid placed between them which can control the flow of electrons when it's electrically charged.

name: Rochelle Salts(KNaC4H4O6·4H2O )
notes: A salt that exhibits piezoelectricity that can be used in gramophone pick-ups, microphones, earpieces and speakers. Can be grown using wine crystals and seaweed.

name: Microphone
notes: A device that converts sound to an electrical signal. Also works the other way, as an earpiece or speaker

name: Cell Phone(SENKU'S PHONE)
notes: A portable telephone that can make and receive calls over a particular radio frequency within a certain range.

name: Land Line
notes: A communication device connection between two or more points using a dedicated physical cable.

name: Speaker
notes: A device that converts an electrical audio signal into a corresponding sound. Can also be used as a microphone.

name: Bone Needle
notes: A needle made of bone, used for sewing or as a record player's needle.

name: Record Player
notes: A device for the mechanical recording and reproduction of sound. Used in Gen and Senku's scheme to play Lillian's last song to the members of the Tsukasa empire.

name: Instant Ramen
notes: A freeze-dried version of the ramen from before, useful as a high-calorie yet low weight meal for the road that only needs hot water. Anime-only, from Episode 25 .

name: Sound Bombs
notes: Deer bladders filled with Brown's gas (hydrogen and oxygen bubbled out of water via electricity) rigged to explode, creating a loud sound.

name: Stenopeic Glasses
notes: Also known as pinhole glasses , they're used to reduce the amount of light reaching the eye.

name: Magnesium
notes: An alkali metal that burns bright white when ignited. Used in making the flare bullets. [ 7 ]

name: Flash Grenade
notes: A light bulb filled with magnesium that, when turned on, flashes extremely bright.

name: Black Light
notes: A light bulb with tinted glass, producing ultraviolet light. Made by adding nickel and barium to glass, creating Wood's glass .

name: Copper Coil
notes: A coiled copper strip used as a spring in a wind up motor, allowing the glass record to be played back smoothly.

name: Megaphone
notes: Used to amplify a person's voice.

name: Beeswax
notes: Used in the lathe to cast delicate parts easily.

name: Lathe
notes: A machine tool that rotates a workpiece about an axis, allowing it to be carved with precise symmetry.

name: Steam Furnace
notes: The boiler part of the neck-swing engine.

name: Casting Molds
notes: The method of making iron parts by casting wax versions, melting the wax out and then pouring molten iron into the molds. A process known as lost wax casting.

name: Casted Parts
notes: The various parts of the neck-swing engine before assembly.

name: Soldering Iron
notes: A large, pointed iron tool heated on a fire, and uses the heat retained to melt solder (an alloy of lead and tin with a low melting point) and join metal parts. Modern soldering irons are heated with electricity, or less commonly a small internal gas torch.

name: Steam Engine
notes: A machine that transforms the heat energy from burning coal into a rotating force, useful for propelling a vehicle.

name: Bamboo Wheels
notes: Wheels made of woven bamboo, absorbing more shock than solid wooden wheels. Based off of NASA's airless tires. [ 8 ]

name: Automobile
notes: Nicknamed the Steam Gorilla , a car that runs on burning wood allowing the Kingdom to transport the scientific equipment closer to the Tsukasa Empire.

name: Paper
notes: Made from plants boiled in sodium hydroxide. Used to make carbon fibre reinforced polymer shielding.

name: Carbon Fiber Shield
notes: Shielding made by combining thin flexible paper with stiff plastic resulting in lightweight but tough material.

name: Armored Tank
notes: The improved Steam Gorilla with shields, a double engine and bigger wheels to mimic a tank.

name: Sodium Hypochlorite
notes: Also known as bleach , a highly corrosive liquid for cleaning, deodorizing and disinfecting. Used to weaken the rope binding the bars in Chrome's jail cell. Suggested by Mecha Senku as an alternative to sodium hydroxide to fans wanting to try making paper.

name: Glue
notes: A tacky substance that Yuzuriha used to stick together shattered statues.

name: Tank
notes: The final form of the Steam Gorilla, with a rupture disk gun.

name: Rupture Disk Cannon
notes: A cannon that fires using water electrolysis where the resulting hydrogen and oxygen buildup inflates the rupture disk. When it breaks, the pressure is released and fires the projectile. It cannot be fired again without first replacing the disk. Anime version also uses an electric spark to detonate the gas, rather than just using the accumulated pressure.

name: Bluff Bullet
notes: A projectile that explodes on contact, creating a showy explosion. Made from a hollow metal can, filled with a fuel mixture that includes coal ash and alcohol, and a glass jar coated with iron powder, filled with sulfuric acid. Upon impact, the glass breaks and the reaction of the acid with the iron ignites the fuels producing a dramatic yet not very powerful explosion.

name: Shock Cannon
notes: A copper sheet in the shape of a paraboloid designed to focus soundwaves in one direction.

name: Nitroglycerin
notes: A dense, colorless, oily, explosive liquid used to force a stalemate in the battle for the Cave of Miracles.

name: Paper Airplane
notes: A glider made of a sheet of paper. Based on the Guinness world record holder design for longest flight.

name: Dynamite
notes: An explosive made of nitroglycerin, sorbents (such as powdered shells or clay) and stabilizers. Used to break the bedrock while digging for Mirai's statue.

name: Stun Gun
notes: A device which delivers an electric shock aimed at temporarily disrupting muscle functions and/or inflicting pain without usually causing significant injury. Made from repurposed telephone parts. Used to defeat Hyoga.

name: Medical Adhesive
notes: A medical-grade instant bonding agent. Made by mixing vinegar, chlorine and sulfur to make chloroacetic acid, then reacting it with sodium cyanide made from blood and iron to get cyanoacetic acid. Add sodium hydroxide to get sodium chloroacetate, then add liquor and formaldehyde to ethyl cyanoacetate to get ethyl cyanoacrylate. Often known as CA glue.

name: Medical Needle
notes: A curved metal needle, perfect for suturing.

name: Blood Bag
notes: A container filled with blood to make up for the blood Tsukasa lost in the fight.

name: Refrigerator
notes: A machine made using two cylinders from the steam gorilla engine, using the force from a water wheel to compress and expand air in different places, it manages to move heat from one place to another, allowing it to cool the inside of a thermally insulated chest. Works like a Stirling Engine ran in reverse, rather than the refrigeration cycle used by modern refrigerators and air conditioners. Used to preserve Tsukasa's body for a future resurrection attempt involving petrification.

name: Thermometer
notes: A glass vial filled with an amount of mercury, marked with graduated lines to show temperature.

name: Dragos Printing Stamp
notes: A stamp used to print Dragos currency

name: Dragos
notes: A currency created by Ryusui to facilitate trade and commerce.

name: Hemp
notes: Raw hemp for making fabrics

name: Spindle
notes: A spike with a weighted end used to twist fibers together to make yarn.

name: Hemp Thread
notes: A thin strand of spun hemp, used for sewing or weaving.

name: Loom
notes: A device used to weave cloth and tapestry.

name: Woven Cloth
notes: A flexible material made by creating an interlocking network of yarns or threads. Used in clothing and the balloon part of the hot air balloon.

name: Woven Clothing
notes: Outfits made from hemp cloth rather than leathers, closer to modern clothing.

name: Hot-air Balloon
notes: A lighter-than-air aircraft consisting of a bag which contains heated air with a basket suspended underneath to carry passengers.

name: Weather Balloon
notes: A Leather balloon filled with hydrogen to test the winds.

name: Playing Cards
notes: A set of playing cards Gen uses for his tricks.

name: Wheat
notes: Raw wild wheat for baking

name: Thresher
notes: Thresher used to separate grain and hay

name: Hoe
notes: Used to tilt the soil allowing for easier seeding

name: Litmus Paper
notes: Paper soaked in crushed morning glories that changes colour according to pH.

name: Bread
notes: First attempt at making bread resulting in industrial waste

name: Bola
notes: Hunting tool used for capturing animals

name: Goat Milk Butter
notes: Butter made by agitating goat's milk and scooping off the top layer.

name: Bread Oven
notes: An oven designed for baking bread at high temperatures in an airtight way (by adding steam).

name: Long Lasting Bread
notes: A delicious wheaten loaf.

name: Steam Gorilla Level 2
notes: Upgraded steam gorilla now able to go up hill thanks to double piston engine.

name: Mirror
notes: A smooth reflective surface made by mixing sodium hydroxide, silver and ammonia, soaking glass in it, adding a dash of glucose and then finally gluing paper or carbon to the back of it. Used in the Daguerreotype cameras.

name: Daguerreotype Camera
notes: A handheld camera used for taking long exposure photographs.

name: Photograph
notes: An image captured on the surface of the Daguerreotype's mirror film after running mercury then a sulfur solution over it.

name: Aerial Photography
notes: Photography designed for survey

name: Scythe
notes: Tool used for harvesting grains

name: Crude Oil
notes: A naturally occurring, yellowish-black liquid found beneath the Earth's surface and can be refined into various types of fuels. The Kingdom's current source is the Sagara oil field. Used to make gasoline.

name: Matches
notes: A easy source of fire, most likely Strike Anywhere type made from red phosphorus

name: Oil pump
notes: Pump made for extraction of oil

name: Stirling Engine
notes: A heat engine that is operated by the cyclic compression and expansion of air or other gas at different temperatures, resulting in a net conversion of heat energy to mechanical work. [ 9 ]

name: Motorboat
notes: An engine-powered boat that uses a propeller rather than sails to move.

name: Gasoline
notes: Refined oil. The so called "Love Drug" mentioned in chapter 1 was gasoline refined from the plastic bottle caps. The molecular structure of polyethylene resembles long chains of "gasoline" molecules stuck together. Chopping the chains into smaller hydrocarbons produces a usable fuel.

name: Signal Tower
notes: A tall tower that emits strong radio waves, powered by a waterwheel attached to a waterfall. Used to determine position with the GPS.

name: GPS
notes: A navigation system that uses fixed points relative to the Earth to determine location. Used by the Kingdom of Science to find their bearings while globetrotting.

name: Braun Tube
notes: Also known as a cathode-ray tube , it is a vacuum tube containing one or more electron guns, the beams of which are manipulated to display images on a phosphorescent screen. Made by taking an Erlenmeyer flask, dissolving powdered sphalerite in water and painting the bottom of the flask and turning it into a vacuum tube. An electron beam is then added, making electrons hit the painted side and light it up. Two crystal plates are then aligned and have voltage passed through them, forcing the electrons into a line.

name: Radar
notes: Made by taking the Braun tube and connecting the radio antenna to two more parallel crystal plates, perpendicular to the first two.

name: Sonar
notes: Made by changing the radar's input from antenna to microphone and using tuning forks.

name: Metal Detector
notes: An instrument to detect the presence of metal using "elektro-magneticky waves" (electromagnetic waves) thanks to a magnetised coil.

name: Digging Rig
notes: Big contraption designed to help with digging up deep ore deposits

name: Hardhat
notes: A yellow protective head gear, used in the mines

name: Rails
notes: Rails used to build the minecart system in the mine

name: Mine Cart
notes: A cart on rails, used to transport cargo around a mine.

name: Asphalt
notes: Used to make smooth roads by mixing gravel and asphalt (oil byproduct) in a 9:1 ratio and then smashing it down smooth.

name: Distillation tower
notes: A big steel tower, designed for distilling oil into usable products

name: Model Ship
notes: A 1:48 ratio scale model of the Perseus to be scaled up to full size.

name: Pantograph
notes: A mechanism for copying movements using parallelograms. Used to copy out the parts of the model ship to full sized pieces.

name: Snowboard
notes: A carbon snowboard

name: Artifical Chocolate
notes: Chocolate produced using chemical processes and not coco beans.

name: Rotary Kiln
notes: A large insulated chamber attached to a huge furnace. The kiln gets fed whatever is in the furnace along with oxygen produced by electrolysis, which makes impurities like phosphorous and silicon float to the top and are filtered out. Burning charcoal then saps the iron ore of its oxygen, making pure iron settle on the bottom.

name: Lathe (Level 2)
notes: Intermediate lathe to make level 3

name: Lathe (Level 3)
notes: Lathe designed to work with steel

name: Bug Net
notes: A net designed for capturing silk moths for production of silk

name: Silk Swimsuits
notes: Bathing outfits made from silkworm thread.

name: Automated Camera Timer
notes: A timing devices that uses the flow of water filling a bamboo pipe to hit a switch, making the camera take a picture.

name: Perseus
notes: A large seafaring vessel.

name: Scopolamine
notes: An autonomic-nerve inhibitor extracted from Datura Metel flowers.

name: Magnifying Glass
notes: A handheld polished convex lens used to magnify objects.

name: Microscope
notes: A device used to examine objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye.

name: Chloroacetone
notes: A colourless liquid with a pungent odour. Used as tear gas. To make it, take baked tree sap and cook it with shells to make acetone, then combine with chlorine.

name: Skatole
notes: The primary contributor to fecal odor. Can be made by combining rotting meat with jasmine then applying heat, or alternatively making very strong jasmine tea and pouring it over heated meat.

name: Shampoo&Conditioner
notes: The shampoo is a lathering soap made from coconut oil, salt, sodium hydroxide and sulfuric acid, used to wash hair. The conditioner is a combination of honey, coconut and lemon used to smooth down hair cuticles.

name: Foundation
notes: A combination of white, yellow and red powders used to even out skintone.

name: Perfume&Lipstick
notes: Various other makeup tools.

name: Wireless Earpiece
notes: A device used to listen in on radiowaves without the need for batteries, known as a crystal radio . Can be made by wrapping copper wire into a coil, attaching a small rock to the middle then adding a piece of Rochelle salt.

name: Motor
notes: A motor that spins using electric current and a magnet. Used to build little rat-like cars.

name: Plaster
notes: A "silent bomb" made by mixing two substances.

name: Platinum
notes: A very rare metal.

name: Nitric Acid Setup
notes: A chemistry setup designed to turn ammonia solution and shells into nitric acid. [ 10 ]

name: Air Pump
notes: A crank-style pump for pumping air into the oxygen tanks.

name: Oxygen Tank
notes: Metal cylinders filled with air with over 50 ATM worth of pressure, equivalent to about 10 minutes of oxygen.

name: Propeller Blade
notes: Feathers coated in plastic.

name: Ball Bearings
notes: Smooth, equally-sized metal balls.

name: Drone (Level 1)
notes: A simple, unstabilised drone capable of flight.

name: Folding Weapon
notes: A foldable polearm-type weapon that allows Moz to keep it hidden.

name: Pistol
notes: A revolver pistol with an unusual barrel rotation style.

name: Carbon Wire
notes: Rope made of spun tar (dregs from burning coal).

name: Drone (Level 2-3)
notes: The previous drone but with an additional propellor and motor, controlled by 4 separate potentiometers.

name: Potentiometer
notes: Coil-based variable resistor that allows the voltage to change based on how far apart the sliding switches are.

name: Dry Lubricant
notes: A combination of graphite (from chimney soot) mixed with alcohol, reducing friction thanks to the carbon's lattice.

name: Petrification Device
notes: Also known as the Petrification Weapon or Medusa , the device that causes petrification .

name: Parabolic Antenna
notes: An antenna that collects radio and sound waves.

name: Constrution Crane
notes: A crane is a machine used to move materials both vertically and horizontally, utilizing a system of a boom, hoist, wire ropes or chains, and sheaves for lifting and relocating heavy objects within the swing of its boom. The device uses one or more simple machines, such as the lever and pulley, to create mechanical advantage to do its work. Cranes are commonly employed in transportation for the loading and unloading of freight, in construction for the movement of materials, and in manufacturing for the assembling of heavy equipment.(appear in anime only episode 56)

name: Wind Mill
notes: A windmill is a machine operated by the force of wind acting on vanes or sails to mill grain (gristmills), pump water, generate electricity, or drive other machinery. (appear in anime only episode 56)

name: Zeolite
notes: It's like a desiccant, a hygroscopic substance used as a drying agent.(appear in anime only episode 56)

name: Hyggrometer
notes: An instrument that measures humidity: that is, how much water vapor is present(appear in anime only episode 56)

name: Fireworks
notes: Fireworks are low explosive pyrotechnic devices used for aesthetic and entertainment purposes. They are most commonly used in fireworks displays (also called a fireworks show or pyrotechnics), combining a large number of devices in an outdoor setting. Such displays are the focal point of many cultural and religious celebrations(such as being a symbol of hope & prayer, to chase away bad spirits and soth the good soul of family and friends), though mismanagement could lead to fireworks accidents.(appear in anime only episode 56)

name: Planetarium
notes: A hut with a globe inside that Kaseki and Yuzuriha built together.

name: Voice Recorder
notes: Based off of phonograph cylinders, used for recording sound. [ 11 ]

name: Gum Syrup
notes: A drink sweetener, normally made of sugar and water, with some gum arabic as an emulsifier. For Senku's version, wash wheat flour and massage it to separate the starch. Then add a few drops of sulfuric acid, boil it for a while and add some witherite (BaCO 3 ). Mix until the pH won't kill you.

name: Calpico
notes: A drink made of strained yogurt mixed with gum syrup and lemon juice.

name: Wort
notes: The liquid extracted from the mashing process during the brewing of beer or whisky. Made by soaking then roasting and drying wheat, removing the unwanted parts, smashing it to dust and finally dissolving in water and filtering it. Adding hops and waiting will make beer.

name: Calcite
notes: Also known as a sunstone when carved, it is a mineral with an optical property called birefringence (double refraction), causing objects viewed through a clear piece of calcite to appear doubled. [ 12 ]

name: Gator Burger
notes: A large hamburger that uses alligator meat for the patties.

name: Calcium Carbide (CaC2)&Acetylene
notes: Calcium carbide is a compound usually used to make acetylene and calcium cyanamide. Acetylene Gas can be made by mixing water and calcium carbide, and can ruin engines if sucked inside. Can also be used as fuel for gas welding.

name: War Table
notes: A board with tiles and figures for planning strategic moves.

name: Ice Cream
notes: A deliciously sweet cold treat for pulling enemy spies to your side. Made by stirring and chilling milk, sugar and kudzu powder and flavoring with vanilla essence. For the synthetic version of vanilla: wrap copper around a test tube, sticking a piece of iron inside and running electricity through it to generate ozone, then take bay laurel extract and boiling in sodium hydroxide before finally infusing the ozone inside.

name: Dilatant Body Armor
notes: A mixture of a fine powder and a liquid creating a dilatant non-Newtonian fluid. In layman's terms, it gets harder the harder you hit it.

name: Drill
notes: A shovelling device for quickly digging underground tunnels, designed by Chrome.

name: Stethoscope
notes: A tool for listening to the functions in a patient's chest.

name: Syringe
notes: A tool for drawing in and expelling fluids via a needle on the end.

name: Aircraft Carrier
notes: The Perseus remade as an aircraft carrier with an on-deck plane catapult for takeoff.

name: Aircraft
notes: An airplane stolen from the Americans originally in chapter 150, finally fixed.

name: Wheelbarrow
notes: A single-wheeled container for easily moving heavy or unwieldy things.

name: Castor Bean Oil
notes: An improved fuel for engines made with castor beans.

name: Bomb&Rocket Sled
notes: Chrome's quick escape plan using a sled on rails and an explosive.

name: Xeno's Boat
notes: A ship stolen from Xeno's castle.

name: Super Soap Bubbles
notes: Big bubbles used for modelling the petrification beam.

name: Spinnaker
notes: A large three-cornered sail attached to the front of the boat.

name: Decoy Ship
notes: The amphibious mobile lab repurposed as a decoy, covered in things that will help it show up on radar.

name: Rubber
notes: Harvested latex mixed with vinegar and kneaded with sulfur powder on high temperatures(140°C-160°C) of mixture[Vulcanization]. Used to make tires, bouncy balls and boots.

name: Tires
notes: Improved wheels by mixing rubber with carbon powder, heating it gently and molding it to shape. Includes a stiffer outer covering with cloth and wires, an inflated inner tube and an axle in the center.

name: Motorcycle
notes: A two-wheeled vehicle capable of traversing rough terrain and carrying up to three passengers.

name: Fax
notes: A method of transferring information via telephone, in this case an image. Basically a Human Fax Machine contraption, similar to how Fax works.

name: Wristwatch
notes: A device worn on the wrist used to tell time (This specific wristwatch can also receive radio signals and convey audible sound).

name: Watchmaker's Loupe
notes: A small magnifying glass worn over an eye, usually used by watchmakers and other appraisers for seeing small details.

name: Ropeway
notes: A method used to transport people and goods across difficult terrain using pulleys and rope.

name: Tin Can Telephone
notes: A string attached to two solid containers to amplify sound travelling through the rope.

name: Rubber Boots
notes: Tall boots to protect travellers in the rainforest from nasty bugs.

name: Animal Repellant
notes: A topical lotion to repel any animals in the rainforest. Made by mixing ethanol and army ants.

name: Brass Knuckles
notes: A piece of metal designed to fit around the hand, in this case specifically concentrated in a point for easily destroying petrification devices.

name: Stealth Vessel
notes: A ship with angled faces designed to reflect radar waves away from rather than back towards their source. It is then improved by covering it with petrification devices, as they do not get picked up by radar.

name: Diamond
notes: Tiny man-made diamonds, created using methanol heated with a tungsten filament. The contraption behind the methanol bottle ensures that the methanol vapor pressure removes any other reactive gases(especially O2) and the burners constant flame indicates that only methanol remains in the 1st bottle. The water trough under methanol bottle provides thermal energy and ensures a steady state for the whole system to process. Natural diamonds were later mined and shaped using a man-made diamond rasp.

name: Elevator
notes: A ropeway, but vertical.

name: Tripwire Trap
notes: A trap triggering a sound recording to play back when the tripwire is touched. When the circuit closes the battery rotates the phonograph cylinder, the reading needles have a magnet attached that transmits a weak electric signal through the wire, the triodes and the copper wire transformers amplify the signal to the speaker to be turned into audible sound.

name: Underwater Waterwheel
notes: A waterwheel that is fully underwater and thus mostly hidden. It is attached to a grindstone that'll be used to grind diamonds.

name: Cart
notes: A 2-wheeled cart constructed by Suika to help carry her petrified friends :).

name: Fish Trap
notes: A woven basket trap for catching fish made by Suika. Likely based off the bottle/pot trap design.

name: Cryogenic Air Separation Unit
notes: A cryogenic fractional distillation device used to separate air into its components. Works by modulating the pressure and temperature of air, and air is separated by exploiting different liquefaction temperatures of oxygen, nitrogen and argon. Used to acquire argon.

name: Argon
notes: A noble gas found in the Earth's atmosphere. Used in the Geiger counter.

name: Geiger Counter
notes: An instrument used for detecting and measuring ionizing radiation. Can also be used to find certain ores. Whenever a beta particle or gamma ray passes through the brass tube in the middle, an electron gets knocked off an argon atom, which then is recieved by anode wire in the centre of the tube while there is a cylindrical cathode along the inner surface of brass tube. This potential difference is quickly amplified and registered by surrounding devices.

name: Ilmenite Ore
notes: A black iron-titanium oxide, the primary ore of titanium. The titanium is to make high-performance alloys for aerospace, military, industrial, medical and other uses.

name: Molybdenite
notes: A mineral of molybdenite sulfide. The molybdenum is used to make steel alloys, particularly superalloys and high-strength ones.

name: Chrome Ore
notes: Also known as chromite , it is a crystalline mineral composed primarily of iron(II) oxide and chromium(III) oxide compounds. The chromium is used to make stainless steel and chrome plating.

name: Pyrochlore Ore((Na,Ca)2Nb2O6(OH,F))
notes: A source of niobium, used in many different scientific applications.

name: Nickel Ore
notes: Used in many different types of alloy.

name: Stainless Steel
notes: A group of ferrous alloys that contain a minimum of 11% chromium. Usually include other elements for different alloy properties. Used to make cans and rust-resistant tools.

name: Mond Process Setup
notes: A technique used to process and purify nickel. Carbon monoxide is introduced to impure nickel at 50°C-60°C, which forms Nickel Tetracarbonyl after binding with pure nickel, which is decomposed in another chamber at 220°C-250°C, giving off pure nickel whereas the CO rejoins the loop using another pipe.

name: Gas Tank
notes: A spherical tank used for storing gas (specifically biofuel). An angular polyhedron(imperfect sphere) is filled with water, and an internal explosion at the center is created with explosives(TNT), the shockwave/pressure creates an almost perfect sphere.

name: Induction Furnace
notes: Used to melt metals into superalloy, here more specifically as a step towards making Inconel Induction Furnace ensures that no atmospheric air comes in contact with the metals, since their reaction can hinder the formation of alloys, vacuum vents are used to remove any trapped oxygen and nitrogen.

name: Fischer-Tropsch Reactor
notes: Fischer-Tropsch is a process used to create biofuel(petrol, diesel, kerosene and other Hydrocarbons) using natural gas made from organic waste/material. Natual gas is made into Syngas(CO+H2) by gasification, which is fed into this reactor that uses metals like Fe/Co as catalyst to produce different lenghts of Hydrocarbons, these are then distilled to separate the fuels.

name: Inconel
notes: A superalloy used for rocketry. Made from a combination of nickel, chrome, molybdenum, iron, titanium and niobium. The Inconel variant here is Inconel-625

name: Level 1 Rocket Engine
notes: A gas turbine engine, later used for the New Perseus . The fuel used for testing is FT-SPK(Fischer-Tropsch Synthetic Paraffinic Kerosene) obtained from the previously distilled biofuels.

name: New Perseus
notes: Fitted with the superalloy engine provides 10k horsepower and speed of 20 knots, making it 5 times faster than Old Perseus.

name: Air Conditioner
notes: A machine for cooling the air, commonly known as "A.C.".

name: Freezer
notes: An improved version of the refrigerator, for keeping food even cooler.

name: Millstone
notes: Used for crushing olives into a paste.

name: Centrifuge
notes: A device that separates the spun contents into its components. Used to extract the oil from the crushed olive paste.

name: Olive Oil
notes: A fragrant oil made of pressed olives, used in various dishes such as ajillo and churros.

name: Dragos Hard Currency
notes: Coins made of superalloys depicting members of the Kingdom of Science, allowing them to pay the people they revive in Europe.

name: Fluorite
notes: A fluorescent mineral found in Barcelona. Used to make better telescope lenses.

name: Fluorite Lens&Telescope
notes: A telescope that uses fluorite lenses to lessen chromatic aberration and distortion.

name: Test Rocket/Missile(Dr. 1)
notes: A rocket for testing Xeno's new jet engine, filled with dynamite and used to blow a path through the dam blocking the Suez Canal.

name: Trowel
notes: A small handheld shovel for digging.

name: Parametron
notes: A simpler replacement circuit for semiconductors in a computer. Made from copper and zinc baked into a donut and wrapped with wire.

name: Adder Circuit
notes: A circuit used to complete basic addition. Both a half adder and full adder were made.

name: Fax Machine
notes: A combination scanner-printer used to send images over radio.

name: Chessboard
notes: A board and set of pieces used for playing chess.

name: Magnetic Memory
notes: A grid of wires and magnets used to store data.

name: Nixie Tubes
notes: A gas-filled bulb with wires set into shapes of numerals so they can be displayed easily.

name: Calculator
notes: A device used to complete mathematical operations.

name: Bauxite
notes: An ore containing several minerals and is the main source of aluminum for aluminum manufacturing.

name: Hardcover Book(Mathematics by SAI)
notes: A book bound and with a hard cover.

name: Theodolite
notes: A device used for measuring angles on the horizon.

name: Archemedes' Screw
notes: A screw for raising water or sand-like materials to a higher level. Used in rice paddy irrigation.

name: Rice Transplanter
notes: Used to plant rice seedlings into a rice paddy, created by modifying the mobile lab.

name: Phosphorite
notes: A mineral rich in phosphorus, used in making fertilizer. Harvested on the island of Nauru due to the presence of many albatrosses.

name: Rice Harvester
notes: A machine used to harvest rice efficiently, made by modifying the mobile lab.

name: Dam
notes: A large-scale dam for producing hydroelectric power. Includes bamboo-reinforced concrete. Controls the flow of a body of water through a giant turbine to generate electricity.

name: Rocket Launchpad
notes: A pad to launch a rocket from, built on Treasure Island.

name: Marionette
notes: A puppet made by Gen ressembling Senku to help catch newly-revived people up with the state of the world so far.

name: Television
notes: A CRT screen for displaying images.

name: Computer(SAL 9000)
notes: The completed moon mission computer. Has the same sepecifications as the Famicom: 16-bit, 60khz CPU, and a memory of 129 core units with 512K ROM and 16K SRAM. Uses punch cards for data processing and programming. Has several classic video games programmed by Sai, including chess and a flight simulator.

name: Perseus D. Monkey
notes: A smaller hybrid ship for short-distance travel around Japan. The name of the ship is a reference to the manga One Piece , specifically the name of the main character Monkey D. Luffy .

name: Selenium
notes: From selenium-bearing silver ore naumannite (Ag 2 Se) found in the Kagoshima prefecture of Japan. Used in the photoconductive surface for the TV camera.

name: Arsenic (As)&Tellurium
notes: From the skarn deposit found in chapter 56. Used in the photoconductive surface for the TV camera.

name: TV Camera
notes: A camera able to convert images it "sees" to an electronic signal that can then be relayed via cables to a separate screen.

name: Large Telescope
notes: The best telescope the Kingdom of Science has on Earth.

name: Solar Panel
notes: Made by layering sheets of copper, selenium, and gold, topped with a layer of glass coated in magnesium fluoride to prevent reflections.

name: Rocket Launch Site
notes: A launch site built on Treasure Island for the rockets. Easily accessible by water.

name: Unmanned Rocket
notes: The first rocket to be tested by the Kingdom of Science. Failed due to the thermal insulation being corroded by gas which poked a hole in the nozzle, resulting in it toppling into the water.

name: Level 99 Rocket Engine
notes: The highest level of rocket engine built by Xeno.

name: Unmanned Rocket
notes: The second test rocket. Exploded due to faulty wiring.

name: Unmanned Rocket
notes: The third test rocket. Failed to launch due to an air bubble vaporizing in the fuel.

name: Unmanned Rocket
notes: The seventh test rocket. Successfully delivered its payload of an Earth reconnaissance satellite into orbit.

name: Satellite
notes: A reconnaissance satellite in orbit around Earth able to send images of the surface of the globe. Orbits at a height of 25,000 km.

name: Space Telescope
notes: A satellite telescope focused on scanning the Moon's surface.

name: Voting Machine
notes: A set of buttons attached to SAL 9000 for counting private votes. Used when voting for whether or not to make the moon mission one-way or two-way.

name: Undersea Cables
notes: Copper wire coated in layers of nickel/steel/aluminum alloy, eucommia elastomer, and steel allowing it to hold up underwater. Used for internet communication.

name: Internet
notes: A network of cables across the globe connecting all the main population hubs.

name: E-paper
notes: A CRT screen that also scans for a light-emitting pen allowing the user to drag a cursor across the screen, similar to the surface of a tablet. Used to ease rocket construction over the internet.

name: Rocket Seat
notes: A large cushioned chair for the astronauts to sit in when going to the moon.

name: Model Rocket
notes: A small scale model rocket of Chrome's 5-part design. Built by Kaseki and Ryusui.

name: Resurrection Watch
notes: A watch built by Joel that sprays revival fluid over the wearer after a set duration of time. Contains one "dose" of fluid.

name: Grenade-Net Launcher
notes: A rocket launcher type of weapon that fires a bullet that opens up into a net covered with grenades. Used to destroy piles of petrification devices.

name: Moving Target Range
notes: A firing range for training the astronauts to shoot moving targets.

name: Lighter
notes: A lighter made by Xeno for his very close friend Stanley, based on the one he had before the first petrification.

name: Dress Forms
notes: Body casts made by Yuzuriha to accurately fit the space suits to the wearers.

name: Silicone Rubber
notes: An easily shaped polymer suitable for a wide range of uses. Used in the space suits.

name: Polyvinyl Chloride
notes: A synthetic plastic polymer with a wide range of uses. Used in the space suits as vinyl and for making plastic wrap.

name: Microwave Oven
notes: An electric oven consisting of a metal box with a high-powered vacuum tube known as a cavity magnetron. Used to heat food quickly.

name: Plastic Wrap
notes: A very thin sheet of polyvinyl chloride used to keep food fresh.

name: Washing Machine
notes: A rotating drum used to wash clothing easier.

name: 8mm Video Camera
notes: A film-based video camera that uses 8 mm wide film to store images.

name: Mini Fridge
notes: A small refrigerator. The name is a parody of "Smeg", a kitchenware brand.

name: Game Console
notes: A Senku-branded game console based of the not-yet-released PS5.

name: Liquid Crystal Display
notes: A screen made by layering different materials, forcing light to align in such a way that can be controlled by electricity.

name: Smartphone
notes: A 40 kg device with a small handheld display, allowing the user access to their email, text, and play video games.

name: Moon Rocket
notes: A rocket destined for the moon.

name: Space Suits
notes: Space suits designed for getting the petrified passengers up into space. Mostly hard shell.

name: Chewable Cigarettes
notes: Chewable tobacco in the shape of cigarettes made by Xeno for Stanley to be used in space.

name: Space Ramen
notes: Ramen designed by Francois to be rehydrated and eaten in space. Used a spray drying system for preparing the packets.

name: Capacitors&Transistors
notes: Electrical components used on printed circuit boards.

name: Space Suits
notes: Softer space suits designed for extravehicular activities such as roaming about on the moon.

name: Medusa Capsule
notes: An airtight capsule with a radio receiver and speaker inside, allowing the astronauts to activate the device even in a vacuum. Later updated to act in reverse, keeping the vacuum inside with the speaker on the outside. [ 13 ]

name: Lunar Rover
notes: A vehicle for traveling quickly across the moon's surface.

name: Passenger Plane
notes: A large airplane for carrying cargo and passengers across oceans.

name: Church Bell
notes: A large bell in a tower.

name: Balloons
notes: Decorative balloons used at Taiju and Yuzuriha's wedding, probably filled with helium.

name: Time Machine
notes: The frame for a time machine. Non-functional.

name: Fake Blood
notes: Fake blood made by Gen from crushed grapes and stored in small packets.

name: Kudayari
notes: A very flexible spear with a hollow metal tube that allows the spear to be twisted during thrusting. Hyoga's favoured weapon.

name: Haber-Bosch Plant
notes: A factory that makes ammonia. Can be used to make unlimited amounts of gunpowder, ammunition or revival fluid using only air and water.

name: Machine Gun
notes: A powerful gun that can fire many times a second.

name: Cigarette
notes: Tobacco rolled into thin paper for smoking.

name: Polygraph
notes: A variety of instruments used to detect whether someone is lying or not based on blood pressure, pulse, respiration and skin conductivity. Xeno's version involved salt water for conductivity, his arm for pulse, and leaning in to feel any quickening of breath.

name: Tractor
notes: A machine for helping around the farm.

name: Landing Strip
notes: A tarmac surface for safely and smoothly landing aircraft.

name: Headset
notes: A device worn over the ears with an attached microphone, allowing the user to both hear and record sounds.

name: Sniper Rifle
notes: A powerful gun with a long range. Has a telescopic sight (also known as a scope) attached to give an accurate point of aim.

name: Binoculars
notes: A device allowing the user to see distant objects clearly.

name: Weather Vane
notes: A device used to measure the speed and direction of wind.

name: Yardstick Dress
notes: A dress with alternating 5-inch-wide lines used to measure the distance to the target.

name: Encryption Device
notes: A device used to scramble messages.

name: Disc Changer
notes: Similar to a jukebox, this machine switches out record disks automatically.

name: Oscilloscope
notes: An electronic test instrument that graphically displays varying signal voltages. Can also be used to "see" sound by using the electrical pulses from a microphone.

name: Submarine
notes: A watercraft capable of independent operation underwater. The design is based off of the Nautilus from 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea (1954) . [ 14 ]

name: Ramming Bomb
notes: A bomb on the end of a long protrusion on the prow of the submarine, designed to detonate on contact with the enemy vessel's hull.

name: Grappling Hooks
notes: Hooks with rope, used to climb and/or rappel down steep sides.

name: Grenades
notes: Explosive devices that throw shrapnel to injure the target(s).

name: Turret
notes: A large, stationary gun set up on the deck of the Perseus.

name: Canoe
notes: A lightweight narrow vessel perfect for traversing rivers, covered in branches as camouflage.

name: Safe
notes: An enormous safe requiring two abloy-style keys to be inserted and a handwheel to be turned before opening.

name: Hanging Housing
notes: A large pumpkin suspended in the air as a safe abode for Chelsea while she was survivng alone.

name: Phosphorescent Paint
notes: Paint made from boiled-down sphalerite pebbles. Used to make easily-seen banners spelling H-E-L-P (or H-E-L-L, due to Chelsea's poor eyesight).

name: Soyuz Capsule
notes: The damaged Soyuz capsule used in reentry. Used to store the treasures Byakuya collected over the rest of his life on earth.

name: Soyuz Survival Kit
notes: A kit containing several tools for survival.

name: Abandoned Lifeboat
notes: A rowboat left by the hermit who was living on Treasure Island prior to petrification.

name: Kickball
notes: A simple sewn-leather ball used for playing.

name: Electric Shaver Motor
notes: An electric shaver motor used for making the recorder.

name: Diamond Ring
notes: Darya's diamond ring given to her by Yakov, used to scratch grooves into the glass record.

name: Disc Cutting Lathe
notes: A rotating disk and needle used to cut grooves into the glass record.

name: Record
notes: A glass record containing Lillian's last performance, the voices of the astronauts and a message for Senku.

name: Rei(Version 01)
notes: Version 01 of Rei, conceptual.

name: Rei(Version 23)
notes: Version 23 of Rei.

name: Rei(Version 37)
notes: Version 37 of Rei. First Rei to show verbal communication.

name: Rei+Canadarm
notes: Rei attached himself to the ISS's Canadarm. Canadarm is a giant robotic arm that is used to deploy, manoeuvre, and capture payloads.

name: Laser Gun(Laser Range Finder)
notes: A laser range finder made from Shamil's Test Equipment. Used to measure the ISS orbiting distance from Earth.

name: Oxygen (O2)&Hydrogen
notes: Made by the electrolysis of water.

name: Nitrogen
notes: Collected from propulsion tanks on the outside of the ISS.

name: Carbon
notes: Made from food the Astronauts left aboard the ISS.

name: Dimethylhydrazine (C2H8N2)Nitrous Oxide
notes: Rocket Fuel used by Rei to correct the orbit of the ISS. The oxidizer used in combination with said fuel.

name: Rei(Version 38)
notes: Gas propulsion upgrade. Visibly smoother than Rei 37.

name: Hydrogen Engine
notes: A modified engine for the ISS that uses water as a fuel source.

name: Rei(Version 39)
notes: An improvement as several years had passed.

name: The Reigelion
notes: A rocket ship built from two space suits with a solar cell attached. Piloted by Rei.

name: Rei(Version 40)
notes: Now with the power of 1,000 smartphones.

name: Rei(Version 41)
notes: Now with the power of 3,000 smartphones thanks to the extra parts from collecting the satellites.

name: Giant Lamp
notes: A large light for flashing while crossing over Tokyo, used to signal Byakuya that Rei is still in space.

name: Rei(Versions 47, 53, 54, 55, 87, 109, 192)
notes: Improvements and rebuilds as several years had passed.

name: Commemorative Book
notes: A book to celebrate the 50th time Rei had to replace the solar cells.

name: Solar Power Farm
notes: A large array of solar panels to gather energy.

name: Space-Based Factory
notes: A factory for mass producing hydrogen bomb rockets.

name: Heavy Hydrogen
notes: Also known as deuterium , used in the hydrogen bombs.

name: Remote-Controlled Spaceship Equipped with Hydrogen Bombs
notes: A rocket designed to redirect an asteroid away from the Earth. 4,000 were made.

name: 3D Printer
notes: A giant 3D printer with a large set of physical command discs so the printing can continue for a long time. Used to print a new ISS and later, a series of smaller 3D printers to print Rei again.
